title: Finite-dimensionality of the section-induced scalar action on first additive cohomology
statement: Let f:C → Spec(k) be a smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field k [def-sc-curves]. Let G be a sheaf of abelian groups in coefficient universe u+1 on the small etale site, with natural additive equivalences a_U:G(U) ≃ Γ(U,O_U). Let T be first derived etale cohomology on sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Suppose m is a k-module structure on T(G), and for every c in k a sheaf endomorphism μ_c exists which multiplies sections under a_U by the pullback of c along U → C → Spec(k), and whose map on T(G) is multiplication by c for m. Then T(G), with this given action m, is finite-dimensional over k. There is no positive-characteristic, Frobenius, or surjectivity assertion.

proof.text: Apply the scalar-compatible comparison lem-sc-additive-cohomology-scalar-comparison. For each c choose mu from the scalar-model hypothesis. Its two equalities show that the additive equivalence e satisfies e(c smul x)=c smul e(x), hence gives an injective k-linear map L to ordinary H^1(C,O_C).

Apply the proper-or-affine dichotomy. In the proper case the unit module is quasi-coherent and finite presentation (it is finite locally free); finiteDimensional_H_of_isProper gives finite-dimensional ordinary H^1. Transport across the injective linear map L by FiniteDimensional.of_injective. In the affine case subsingleton_H_succ_of_isAffine applied to the unit module gives zero ordinary H^1; injectivity of e gives a subsingleton source, whose given module is finite-dimensional.
